subject: Throughput sizing follow-up: FinEx post-call
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finex.com>, Priya Sharma <priya@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Throughput sizing follow-up: FinEx post-call

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary workload: user-facing chat + summarization for transactional documents.
- Streaming required for chat responses (token-by-token).
- Latency target: p95 <= 200ms for the chat endpoint; a subset of flows need p95 <= 150ms.
- Typical prompt + history: ~600 tokens on average, peak up to 2.5k tokens (long docs).
- Expected steady-state QPS: ~50 requests/sec; peak burst QPS: ~220 (10–15 minute bursts).
- Concurrency: typical concurrent active users ~40–70, but bursts can push concurrent requests to 300+.

Action items / asks for you: 
1) Can you fill the attached finex-throughput-sizing-sheet.csv with per-endpoint QPS, average tokens in, tokens out, and % streaming required?
2) If possible, share a sample request trace (anonymized) or histogram of request sizes by endpoint.
3) Confirm whether history can be truncated/summary-cacheable for older turns (helps batching).

What we'll do next: 
- We’ll run a quick back-of-envelope sizing from the sheet and propose a pilot config (dedicated capacity + suggested GPU counts).
- Marissa will look at batching/latency knobs specific to streaming.

Attachments: finex-throughput-sizing-sheet.csv (worksheet)

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finex.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya@finex.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 16:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing follow-up: FinEx post-call

Thanks Rafael — great summary. A few clarifications from our side: 
- Average prompt (including history): ~600 tokens; summaries typically add ~120–300 tokens.
- Streaming: yes, chat must stream token-by-token for UX, especially on mobile.
- Latency: p95 200ms is fine for most flows; transaction confirmations need p95 <= 150ms.
- Steady-state QPS ~50 is correct; we see ~5x spikes during settlement windows (hence the 220 peak).

I'll ask procurement (cc'd) to consolidate contract/PO questions — they'll likely want a small pilot first. We'll try to populate your sizing sheet by EOD Tuesday.

-Alex
Alex Turner
Head of Platform Engineering | FinEx Solutions
alex.turner@finex.com
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finex.com>, Priya Sharma <priya@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing follow-up: FinEx post-call

Appreciate the quick reply, Alex. Attached another short doc (redwood-performance-slo-doc.pdf) that outlines assumptions we use for streaming vs non-streaming endpoints and how we translate tokens/sec into GPU sizing.\n
Preliminary assumptions (to align on):
- Model variant: open-model-16b quantized (we can propose alternatives).
- Effective tokens/sec per A100-equivalent GPU (with streaming): ~18k tokens/sec (no KV reuse).
- With aggressive prefix reuse / KV cache we can improve effective tokens/sec by ~15–30% depending on cache hit rate.

Based on the sheet values you gave on the call, high-level pilot suggestion:
- Dedicated pilot: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (allows steady-state headroom + 2x burst capacity with autoscale).
- Target config: enable prefix KV caching + 80% batching window for steady-state flows.

Next steps: once you drop the per-endpoint rows in the sheet I’ll run exact tokens/sec -> GPU estimates and share a short proposal. If you’re open, propose a 60-minute sizing workshop this week where we can go over traces and map endpoints to SLOs.

Link to live sheet: https://drive.google.com/finex-sizing-sheet
Attachments: redwood-performance-slo-doc.pdf

Rafael
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@finex.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya@finex.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing follow-up: FinEx post-call

Quick note from the infra side — two things to check that materially change sizing: 
1) Tokenization / effective token expansion: some document formats expand ~10–20% after tokenization. Please confirm whether your 600-token average is pre- or post-tokenization.
2) Peak vs steady ratio: if peak bursts are short (10–15 minutes), we can rely on burst autoscaling with a different cost profile than sustained capacity; if they’re sustained (>1hr) we should size higher baseline.

If you can share a small sample of anonymized traces (timestamps + request token counts) we can run a 30–60m simulation and return a recommended GPU timeline. Happy to run this with you on the workshop.

—Marissa

Subject: Re: Throughput sizing follow-up: FinEx post-call — workshop scheduling & next steps

Hi Alex / Priya — looping in Neha from our partnerships/eng team to coordinate pilot logistics. Proposed next steps: 
- Sizing workshop: Thu 24 Jun, 10:00–11:00 PT (we can shift if that conflicts). Agenda: review traces, fill gaps in the sheet, run quick simulation, agree pilot KPIs (latency p95, errors, cost target).
- Action item for you: drop the completed finex-throughput-sizing-sheet.csv in the Drive link and, if possible, attach an anonymized 1–2k-request trace (CSV with timestamps + token counts).
- Procurement: trigger the pilot MSA/PO conversation — we can provide a one-month pilot quote for the 4x GPU config above.

We’ll prepare an initial cost/latency estimate ahead of the workshop and share it 24h beforehand. Please confirm the workshop time or propose alternatives.

Thanks — Neha
